strings.name: Kazuo Ueda
strings.role: Economist and Governor of the Bank of Japan
strings.summary: Kazuo Ueda is a Japanese economist who became Governor of the Bank of Japan in 2023. He taught at institutions including the University of Tokyo and served on the BOJ Policy Board from 1998 to 2005. During his governorship, the Board changed the negative-interest-rate and yield-curve-control framework in 2024.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Policy decisions are attributed to the collective Board; decision, effective and speech publication dates are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Through economic research and central bank leadership, participated in adjustments to Japan’s longstanding monetary easing policies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a mathematics bachelor’s degree at the University of Tokyo in 1974 and an economics PhD at MIT in 1980.
strings.facts.f2.label: Governor’s term
strings.facts.f2.value: Took office on April 9, 2023; the official term ends April 8, 2028, a future date rather than completed service.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Research and policy practice
strings.highlights.h1.text: Combined an academic career with central banking, returning to teaching at the University of Tokyo after serving on the Policy Board.
strings.highlights.h2.title: The 2024 framework change
strings.highlights.h2.text: The Board ended the negative-rate and yield-curve-control framework while anticipating continued accommodative financial conditions; this did not end all easing measures at once.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Delivered an IMF lecture
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed Japan’s current account surplus and corporate adjustment; the BOJ published the text on November 7.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Board changed the policy framework
strings.timeline.t2.text: Ueda voted for the new short-term interest-rate guideline; the 0–0.1% overnight rate target took effect on March 21.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became BOJ Governor
strings.timeline.t3.text: Began his governorship following a career in academic research and earlier Policy Board service.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joined Kyoritsu Women’s University
strings.timeline.t4.text: His official biography records his appointment as a professor that month.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Returned to the University of Tokyo
strings.timeline.t5.text: Left the Policy Board and became a professor at the University of Tokyo’s Graduate School of Economics.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined the Policy Board
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began serving on the BOJ Policy Board and was reappointed in April 2000.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earned an economics PhD
strings.timeline.t7.text: After earning his economics doctorate at MIT, joined the University of British Columbia in July that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed undergraduate mathematics studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a mathematics bachelor’s degree at the University of Tokyo before turning to economics.
